1.pericope_label: Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee. For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee. And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising.

schools.summary: Keil and Delitzsch deny that the night over the nations means ignorance or enmity against God, reading it instead as the depth of darkness left after the judgments have passed, a night like the first day's which must give place to light, and asking where the sun will rise, since Zion is the east; Ellicott sees the new Jerusalem under the forms of the old, prostrate as in the darkness below and now bidden rise, the veil still lying over the heathen who are to share her light.

Gill notes the versions that supply the city's name and takes the address for the Jewish church as distinct from the Gentiles who come to it, surveys the darkness of his own day as pagan, Mahometan and papal with the Gospel light on a very small spot, and offers a second construction in which the darkness is the confusion of the antichristian states.

Clarke takes the subject to be the period when Jews and Gentiles become one fold under one Shepherd, thinks the prospect lifted the prophet above even his usual majesty, and alone says the calling of the Gentiles has in some sort already happened; Wesley reads the rising as a Hebrew idiom for recovery out of a servile condition, and finds under the type of the city's restoration the flourishing state of the Gentile church.

Henry works the light in two registers, historically from the return out of captivity and the coming of the Redeemer, and theologically from God as the father and fountain of lights, distinguishing the comfort of his favour when he appears to us from the credit of it when he appears for us.

positions.position: The Jewish church as distinct from the Gentiles, converted at last and called out of a long dejection.
The Gentile church, under a type of the city's restoration.
Both, in the period when Jews and Gentiles become one fold under one Shepherd.
The new Jerusalem, seen in vision under the forms of the old.

debates.question: What is the darkness that covers the earth?

positions.position: Ignorance, idolatry, superstition and false worship, in pagan, Mahometan and papal forms.
The state of the Gentile people.
All kinds of errors.
The veil that had shrouded Zion, still lying over the heathen who are to share her light.
Not a night of ignorance or enmity at all, but the depth of darkness still covering the earth after the judgments have passed.

debates.question: Has the coming of the Gentiles happened yet?

positions.position: In some sort already: they have received the Gospel from that land and their kings have embraced it, though the full completion is reserved for future times.
A plain prophecy of their calling, still to be fulfilled.
Still future: they are to come to the Gospel preached in her midst and into her church state.

outliers.claim: Supplies the governing image by asking where, in a night that must break, the sun will rise, and answering that Zion is the east in which this sun of suns comes up.

Distinguishes two ways the glory is seen: when God appears to us we have the comfort of his favour and the glory rises like the morning, and when he appears for us we have the credit of it and the glory is seen upon us.

themes: Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.
For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.
And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising.

4.pericope_label: Lift up thine eyes round about, and see: all they gather themselves together, they come to thee: thy sons shall come from far, and thy daughters shall be nursed at thy side. Then thou shalt see, and flow together, and thine heart shall fear, and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee. The multitude of camels shall cover thee, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense; and they shall shew forth the praises of the Lord. All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered together unto thee, the rams of Nebaioth shall minister unto thee: they shall come up with acceptance on mine altar, and I will glorify the house of my glory. Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows? Surely the isles shall wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring thy sons from far, their silver and their gold with them, unto the name of the Lord thy God, and to the Holy One of Israel, because he hath glorified thee.

schools.summary: Keil and Delitzsch weigh the external evidence for the disputed verb and keep the reading from to see, mark the throb of delight mingled with trembling, and note that the third movement of the chapter begins here, glorification by the service of the nations; Ellicott gives the eastern custom of carrying a child on the hip, renders the heart's motion as a throb of awe followed by ecstasy, sets the Nabathaean kingdom behind the tribal names, and reads the sea's abundance as the riches of the West.

Gill has the flow of joy like a river's stream, traces the tribes to sons of Abraham and of Ishmael and applies them to the Turks and Saracens who shall now be converted, and takes the cloud four ways at once, for number, elevation, fulness of grace, and unanimity.

Clarke marshals the manuscripts for reading fear rather than see and confirms it from the parallelism, gathers the variants on the doves and the ships, and reports the reading by which the rams offer themselves voluntarily, supported from the heathen notion of a willing victim; Wesley takes the enlargement as joy and love together and types the queen's visit to Solomon.
Henry puts the whole sequence on one ground, that all the favour the people of God find with men is owing to the light of his countenance towards them.

debates.question: Is the reading see or fear?

positions.position: Fear, on forty and twenty-eight manuscripts and on the parallelism, the heart ruffled and dilated answering to fear and joy.
See, which the ancient versions, all the earlier Jewish commentators but one, and the Masoretic text support.
A various reading adopted by many gives fear.

debates.question: Who are the tribes that bring their wealth?

positions.position: Arabians descended from Abraham and Ishmael, and so the Turks and Saracens, to be converted now.
The Nabathaean Arabs and their neighbours, covering what the Roman geographers called the two Arabias.
Countries typified by the queen who visited Solomon and brought her gifts.

debates.question: What is the cloud that flies?

positions.position: The converts themselves, for number, elevation, fulness of grace and unanimity.
The cloud-like sails of the ships bringing the exiles home.
A figure of number and of speed together.

outliers.claim: Reports the reading by which the rams wait for no priest but present themselves freely on the altar, and supports it from the heathen notion that a victim brought without reluctance was a good omen and one that broke away a bad one.

Marks the structure of the chapter, this being where the third movement begins: after glorification by the rising of the glory and by the recovery of the scattered children comes that by the nations' service.

themes: Lift up thine eyes round about, and see: all they gather themselves together, they come to thee: thy sons shall come from far, and thy daughters shall be nursed at thy side.
Then thou shalt see, and flow together, and thine heart shall fear, and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee.
The multitude of camels shall cover thee, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense; and they shall shew forth the praises of the Lord.

All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered together unto thee, the rams of Nebaioth shall minister unto thee: they shall come up with acceptance on mine altar, and I will glorify the house of my glory.
Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows?

Surely the isles shall wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring thy sons from far, their silver and their gold with them, unto the name of the Lord thy God, and to the Holy One of Israel, because he hath glorified thee.

10.pericope_label: And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee. Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought. For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted. The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious. The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.

schools.summary: Keil and Delitzsch have the trees dug up with their roots rather than felled, and mark the turn from what is great in the world of men to what is great in nature, holding that the persecutors are now no more and their children feel themselves disarmed; Ellicott allows the willing proselyte but sets subjection beside it, reads the verb used of the kings as bringing them captive, sees a revival of Solomon's glories in the timber, takes the place of God's feet as parallel with the sanctuary, and prefers the law of inherited retribution to the common explanation.

Gill takes the builders for Gentiles once strangers to the covenants and now converted in great numbers, gives the open gates three senses of peace, concourse and unexhausted capacity, allegorises the trees of Lebanon into men eminent for gifts and graces, and runs through three candidates for the sons of the afflicters.

Clarke identifies the place of God's feet as the ark, over which the appearance the Jews called the shechinah rested and to which a footstool belongs as the appendage of a throne; Wesley says the strangers shall administer all necessaries, allegorises the trees the same way as Gill, and allows that the Hebrew idiom for sons may mean the men themselves.

debates.question: In what spirit do the strangers build and the kings come?

positions.position: As converts made useful in building up and defending the church.
Either as willing proselytes or as brought into subjection, the verb used of the kings implying captives.
As those who administer all necessaries to her.

debates.question: What is the glory of Lebanon?

positions.position: Timber for the buildings, or trees planted in the courts and open places.
Living trees dug up with their roots rather than felled.
Men eminent for gifts and graces, drawn with the cords of love into the church.

debates.question: Why are the sons of the afflicters named rather than the afflicters?

positions.position: Because the persecutors themselves are now no more, and their children feel themselves disarmed.
Not for that common reason, but as an expression of the law of inherited retribution.
Because the Hebrew idiom may mean the men themselves.

outliers.claim: Identifies the place of God's feet as the ark, since the appearance the Jews called the shechinah rested between the cherubim above it, and a footstool is a necessary appendage to a throne.
Gets three senses out of the open gates: a peaceable state with no enemy to fear, a concourse always coming in, and a capacity that is never filled, since however many come there will still be room.

themes: And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.
Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.
For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.
The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious.

The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.

15.pericope_label: Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated, so that no man went through thee, I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations. Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles, and shalt suck the breast of kings: and thou shalt know that I the Lord am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob. For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron: I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness. Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders; but thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise. The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory. Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended. Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified. A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the Lord will hasten it in his time.

schools.summary: Keil and Delitzsch separate the two ideas the name Zion carries and show that one governs the verse about desertion and the other the verse about nursing, and allow the little one to grow by extension of fellowship as well as by children; Ellicott mingles the slighted wife with the ruined city, contrasts the oppressive officers of Solomon's reign with the righteous ones here, recalls the eastern practice of naming city walls after a consecration, reads the violence as internal misgovernment rather than invasion, and takes the little one for a clan rather than a number.

Gill reads the four materials as three dispensations, hears the end of antichristian persecution in the silenced violence, distinguishes the church's own sun of righteousness from the natural sun of the verse before, and refuses to let all righteous be said loosely, since the members of churches never yet were.

Clarke judges the line about the moon defective and would repair it from the Greek and the Aramaic, notes the manuscripts for the reading of my planting, and draws a careful distinction about the hastening; Wesley makes the nations' wealth come as freely as milk from a mother's breast, puts the officers in four words, and dates the whole to the thousand years of Christ's reign on earth.

Henry sets the promise against a city her friends abandoned and her enemies abhorred, and adds the caution that governs the rest, that her excellency was short and came far short of the vast compass of this promise.

debates.question: What does the exchange of materials mean?

positions.position: Three dispensations: wood and stones the old covenant, brass and iron the gospel, silver and gold the glory to come.
The wealth of Solomon's reign, with the difference that his officers were instruments of oppression and these are the embodiment of righteousness.
An allusion to the days when gold was as brass, extending even to the tax-gatherers.
The outward and inward beauty of the city, shown by her materials and by the powers prevailing within her.

debates.question: What violence is it that shall no more be heard?

positions.position: Antichristian persecution, with none left to hurt.
Internal misgovernment rather than external invasion.
Whatever the thousand years of Christ's reign on earth will end.

debates.question: What becomes of sun and moon?

positions.position: They may still shine, but will not be needed in a greater radiance where there is no waning and no setting.
The line is defective and should read by night, on the authority of the Greek and the Aramaic.
The sun of the following verse is not this one at all, but the church's own sun of righteousness, who has risings and settings now but will not have them then.

outliers.claim: Recalls the eastern practice of giving city walls names implying a consecration, and cites the two divine names borne by the walls of Babylon.
Draws a careful distinction about the hastening: the time set must come before anything begins, so it is not the appointed time that is hastened but every circumstance of the event once begun.
